- U3: Push custom module (uber-jar) via REST API to install in cluster

2. State technical/design decisions and assumptions
3. Provide most likely effort estimate per activity (work-hours)
4. Sum total

technical_and_design_decisions: Target platform is Spring Framework 6.x running on Java 17+, built on top of the existing XD-style runtime (stream DSL, source/sink module model, singlenode and distributed containers, pluggable message bus).

U1 (mass ingestion) is implemented as launchable batch job modules rather than streams: a 'jdbc-to-hdfs' job that extracts a table/query via JDBC (paged ItemReader) and writes delimited-text or Avro files to HDFS using the Hadoop FileSystem API with chunked, parallel writes for efficiency, plus HAWQ/GPDB loading implemented via the gpfdist external-table protocol (HTTP-based data server that GPDB segments read in parallel).

Existing open-source components are reused where possible (Spring Batch for job orchestration, Hadoop client libraries, an existing gpfdist protocol implementation) instead of writing everything from scratch.

U2 is executed as a time-boxed spike only: study the Kafka simple (low-level) consumer API (explicit partition assignment, manual offset management, leader failover handling), build a throwaway prototype, and produce a findings document with recommended approach and next steps; no production module is delivered for U2.

U3 is implemented as a new admin REST endpoint (POST /modules, multipart/form-data uber-jar upload) with jar validation (module metadata, size limit, duplicate/version handling), persistence to a shared module repository, and distribution to all containers via ZooKeeper watch events; containers load uploaded modules in isolated classloaders with runtime registry refresh. Existing admin basic authentication is reused; no UI is built.

U5 generator source exposes options numMsgs (default 10000), msgSize (default 1024) and numThreads (default 1); it generates deterministic fixed-size payloads, uses a shared atomic counter across producer threads, sends through the configured message-bus binder with backpressure, and stops cleanly after numMsgs messages.

U6 perf-meter sink exposes option numMsgs (default 1000); it writes a log line (timestamp, cumulative message count, message rate since the previous log event) to the standard container log via SLF4J/Logback every numMsgs messages.

U7 performance measurement runs 'generator | perf-meter' on a singlenode container with 1,000,000 messages of 1000 bytes on one thread; the baseline is measured with the default local singlenode transport and repeated with the Kafka bus provisioned from the U4 sample project for comparison.

U8 test coverage uses JUnit 5 with mocked Kafka clients for unit tests and an embedded Kafka broker (spring-kafka-test / EmbeddedKafkaBroker) for integration tests, wired into the existing CI pipeline as part of the standard build.

U4 is delivered as a standalone GitHub project containing Docker Compose provisioning (ZooKeeper, Kafka, XD admin and containers), topic-creation scripts, configuration for Kafka as message bus and Kafka as source, sample stream definitions, and a step-by-step README.
Build is a Maven multi-module build; deployable modules are packaged as uber-jars carrying module metadata consumed by the XD module registry and the new upload endpoint.
assumptions: An existing XD-style runtime already provides the stream DSL, singlenode/distributed containers, module packaging model, a working Kafka message-bus implementation, and existing Kafka source and sink modules; this increment extends that codebase rather than building it from scratch (U8 and U4 both presuppose existing Kafka modules).

U1 scope is limited to relational databases reachable via JDBC (single table or ad-hoc query extract) into HDFS (delimited text or Avro) and loading into HAWQ/GPDB via gpfdist; 'and others' source types are out of scope for this increment.
The Hadoop/HDFS test environment has no Kerberos or TLS; security integration for Hadoop is out of scope.
U2 delivers only the spike outputs (study, prototype, findings document with approach and next steps); implementing a simple-consumer-based production Kafka source is a future increment.

For U3 there is a single admin server, containers register via ZooKeeper, uber-jars are limited to 100 MB, re-upload of an existing module version is idempotent/rejected with a clear error, and no rolling-upgrade, HA-failover or UI work is included.

Test infrastructure is available: Docker-based Kafka/ZooKeeper locally, hadoop-minicluster for HDFS tests, PostgreSQL/HSQLDB for JDBC tests, a gpfdist protocol mock for automated GPDB/HAWQ tests, and a shared GPDB/HAWQ appliance for occasional manual verification.
An existing CI server (e.g., Jenkins/GitHub Actions) is available; only pipeline configuration is needed.
All work is performed by one developer (myself); figures are work-hours of effort, not elapsed calendar duration.
Unit testing is included within each development activity; integration testing, performance runs, end-to-end verification and documentation are separate activities.
Documentation scope is limited to module reference docs, REST API documentation, the spike findings document, the performance report, and the sample project README.
